text.p: Unitrin Inc said Friday revenues in its property and casualty insurance segment rose to $209.2 million from $194.7 million a year ago.
Unitrin attributed the higher revenues to the January 1997 acquisition of Union Automobile Indemnity Co and to a higher volume of automobile insurance.
Operating profit in the property and casualty segment rose to $16.5 million from $10.6 million a year ago, due primarily to improved storm and other losses.

Revenues in the life and health insurance segment decreased to $144.9 million from $156.6 million due to lower volume of accident and health insurance and the ceding of certain life insurnace policies to third parties.
The life insurance operating profit fell to $10.4 million from $12.7 million due primarily to higher underwriting expenses as a percentage of premiums.

Revenues in the consumer finance segment rose to $32.4 million from $30.1 million. Operating profit, however, fell to $1.0 million from $7.1 million due primarliy to higher provisions for loan losses.
Earlier, Unitrin announced second quarter net earnings of $0.03 a share after an $0.85 charge compared with year-ago earnings of $0.78 a share.
The charge related to its share of Western Atlas Inc's charges for the write-off of in-process research and development activities. Unitrin owns about 24 percent of Western Atlas.
